options: To make the graphs look nice
To keep noise out of the PID
questions.explain: Motor and frame noise must not reach the PID and the motors: D amplifies noise, and the motors heat up.

questions.q: What is the price of any filter?
questions.explain: A filter lags behind the signal: more filtering means a slower response.

questions.q: The most effective motor-noise filter in Betaflight?
questions.explain: The RPM filter puts narrow notches exactly on each motor's frequency using ESC telemetry.

questions.q: What does the dynamic notch do?
options: Doubles D at the peak frequency
questions.explain: The dynamic notch tracks frame resonances and whatever else the RPM filter didn't catch.

options: Only LPF, notches are off by default
questions.explain: First the precise per-motor notches, then the automatic ones, then the final lowpass.

questions.q: The motors are hot after changing the filters. What do you do?
options: Raise P to override the noise
Roll back and look at the spectrum
questions.explain: Heat is a sign of noise getting through. Go back to a working state, then analyze.

questions.q: In what order are the gyro filters applied in Betaflight 4.5?
questions.explain: The order from gyroFiltering(): narrowband notches first, then the LPFs.

options: Disables the RPM filter and enables PT3 instead
questions.explain: 100 is the defaults; higher means less filtering and less delay.

options: Motor peaks ≤ 5–10 dB above the floor
Gyro LPF below 100 Hz on a 5"
questions.explain: A low LPF “hides” mechanics at the cost of delay — that's not a criterion, it's a symptom.

questions.q: The course grader's output for a 5" log. Which conclusion is correct?
questions.fragment:
[FAIL] filters  roll noise after filters: 12.9 (limit <= 4.0 deg/s)
[FAIL] filters  roll noise reduction: 4.4 (limit >= 6.0 dB)
[PASS] filters  roll dominant noise frequency: 250.0
[FAIL] rpm      eRPM telemetry logged: None (limit present)
options: Motor noise (~250 Hz) gets through the filters, and the RPM filter isn't working — there's no eRPM telemetry
The 250 Hz peak is a frame resonance; the RPM filter won't help here, only a static notch will
The filters are too strong: 4 dB of reduction means an over-filtered gyro, they need to be relaxed
The gyro is damaged: 13 °/s of noise after the filters is impossible on a healthy sensor
questions.explain: A peak at the motor frequency, weak reduction and no eRPM point to a non-working RPM filter.
